props.gloss_en: Rav Huna: a foul odour that has a source -- he distances four cubits and reads the Shema
Rav Chisda: he distances four cubits from the place where the odour stopped and reads the Shema
one may not read the Shema facing human excrement, dog excrement, pig excrement, chicken excrement, or a dung-heap whose smell is bad
if it was in a place ten handbreadths high or ten handbreadths low, he sits beside it and reads the Shema
and if not, he distances from it as far as his eyes see
a foul odour that has a source: he distances four cubits from the place of the odour and reads the Shema
the halakha follows this baraita (25a.6) in all these rulings -- which Rava denies (לית הלכתא)
Rava: rather, the halakha follows this [other] baraita
one may not read the Shema facing human excrement, nor pig excrement, nor dog excrement when one put hides into them
come see these mats of the study hall: these sleep and these study
that is for words of Torah; and for words of Torah too, we said it only of another's [odour]
but for the recitation of the Shema, no
but his own [odour] -- no, not even for words of Torah
